attempts.bug_summary: Adjacent expressions occurring after an earlier literal substitution are treated as though they are still part of the substitution. This introduces an unnecessary empty-string concatenation into otherwise independent expressions.

When an escape-prefix character is repeated inside a literal substitution, the implementation treats every prefix after the first as already escaped and does not preserve the required escaping for the generated text literal. This affects substitutions containing consecutive backslashes while leaving ordinary text and single escape prefixes unchanged.

Nested expression unwinding incorrectly marks the parser as being outside an expression when an inner expression closes. This can cause a subsequent nested expression opener to be processed as a top-level expression, corrupting state for nested expression sequences within a substitution.
